definitions.explanation: The energy or force that drives machinery, vehicles, or equipment. Refers to the source of mechanical energy that makes something operate.

examples.japanese: {蒸気|じょうき}を{動力|どうりょく}にする。
examples.english: To use steam as the power source.

examples.japanese: この{船|ふね}は{風力|ふうりょく}を{動力|どうりょく}として{利用|りよう}している。
examples.english: This ship uses wind power as its driving force.

examples.japanese: {電気自動車|でんきじどうしゃ}は{電池|でんち}を{動力源|どうりょくげん}とし、ガソリンを{使|つか}わない。
examples.english: Electric vehicles use batteries as their power source and do not use gasoline.

notes: Common collocations: {動力源|どうりょくげん} (power source), {動力|どうりょく}{装置|そうち} (power unit/drive system), {動力|どうりょく}{伝達|でんたつ} (power transmission), {原子力|げんしりょく}{動力|どうりょく} (nuclear power). Often appears in discussions of engines, industrial machinery, and energy technology. Related: エンジン (engine — the mechanical device itself), {馬力|ばりき} (horsepower — a unit of power), {推進力|すいしんりょく} (propulsive force — emphasizes forward movement).
